problem_text:
A logistics firm seeks to allocate a fleet of specialized delivery vehicles from six regional depots (labeled D1 through D6) to six major urban fulfillment centers (labeled C1 through C6) in order to minimize the total operational expenditure.

The number of vehicles ready for dispatch at each depot is fixed:  
Depot D1 has 92 vehicles available.  
Depot D2 has 115 vehicles available.  
Depot D3 has 173 vehicles available.  
Depot D4 has 125 vehicles available.  
Depot D5 has 136 vehicles available.  
Depot D6 has 79 vehicles available.

The fulfillment centers require precise numbers of vehicles to meet their daily distribution schedules:  
Center C1 must receive exactly 15 vehicles.  
Center C2 must receive exactly 148 vehicles.  
Center C3 must receive exactly 45 vehicles.  
Center C4 must receive exactly 133 vehicles.  
Center C5 must receive exactly 132 vehicles.  
Center C6 must receive exactly 77 vehicles.

The cost per vehicle dispatched from a given depot to a specific center, accounting for distance, tolls, and regional fees, is detailed in the table:

| Depot / Center | C1 | C2 | C3 | C4 | C5 | C6 |
|----------------|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| D1             | 18 | 12 | 3  | 13 | 1  | 9  |
| D2             | 18 | 4  | 15 | 12 | 9  | 19 |
| D3             | 13 | 12 | 4  | 8  | 16 | 1  |
| D4             | 20 | 18 | 11 | 20 | 8  | 3  |
| D5             | 15 | 10 | 14 | 4  | 5  | 2  |
| D6             | 2  | 10 | 16 | 4  | 4  | 8  |

Determine the optimal vehicle allocation plan that satisfies all dispatch availabilities and center requirements while incurring the lowest possible total cost.
